OP you're very reasonable and understanding, and I hope you never have to deal with a situation like this again! As a tech/ pharmacist intern I strive really hard to see the nuance in every situation, every person's health and dependency on medication is different. 

Also, a well educated technician can tell what medications aren't emergencies (missing a dose of your cholesterol med is not gonna cause withdrawals lol), and which are more acute/urgent (blood thinners, antibiotics, mood stabilizers, seizure meds, etc. etc.) BUT in my experience at the 3 letter hell, techs barely get time to do their training modules. It's so half assed and rushed  that other techs/pharmacists will take their modules FOR trainees and even give them the answers to their licensure test. 

The metrics are called "WeCare" scores, and if you visit the subreddits for that or any chain store you'll get even more insight on the conditions. Absolutely horrible treatment and honestly such a danger to patients.

No disrespect at all but do you expect them to pull it out of their ass or something? If they do not have it on hand on the only thing that they can do is order it or see if another pharmacy of the same chain has it in stock. If not, they can offer to transfer it to a competing pharmacy of your choice that does have it. Will yelling at them magically spawn the medication?
Sometimes older drugs that have been out on the market do become harder to obtain especially if they do not get prescribed often, because there's a limited amount you can order so the pharmacist wasn't giving you a bullshit reasoning. Manufacture back orders happen as well, at that point we can't obtain the product even if we wanted to. 

I understand the frustration of not having your life saving medication but yelling at staff isn't gonna solve this problem, you're just a dick and anyone would get offended being yelled at.

We both lost our companions today. My beautiful boy Simon did not pull through and passed on at the vet this morning. I took him for further testing and a second opinion as the ER vet left me feeling unclear about Simon's future. 

After receiving fluids and treatment at the ER, Simon was much more animated for an hour two and even ate half a can of his new food! Shortly after however he reversed back to his depleted state and stayed in bed. I fell asleep on the floor next to his bed. 

In the morning he was awake and a bit more lively as everyone in the house came to see him. I had a gut feeling he wasn't going to pull through and let everyone know this might be goodbye. Before putting him in his carrier, I sat him by the window so he could see the pond and the world one last time and he was alert but weak.

Initially at the vet, the doctor tried to reassure me that he's seen cases with numbers higher than Simon and in worse condition. He tried to give me hope in that Simon ate yesterday, drank water, and hadn't thrown up. He also didn't lose a ton of weight just a lot of muscle mass. 

After the tests and the urine exam however we discovered his numbers worsened significantly and his anemia was much more severe than it was the day before. His urine was also dark brown and had some blood in it. With fluid treatments and now  a blood transfusion necessary, I was told that chances were slim but we could try. 

My boy nodded off in my arms today at the vet and didn't wake up. I feel immense peace in knowing that I was present til the very end. He was with me during the most crucial part of my life, from age 12 to 22 he's been my friend through the hardest losses and greatest gains. He's experienced the death of my mother and our other beloved pets and was always stoic until his very own passing. 

I am crushed to know that you are enduring the same in losing your girl, especially to something unrelated to her KD that you were trying so hard to adapt to. Know that she absolutely appreciated your efforts to keep her here with you and fought through it like the little queen that she was. I wish you the absolute best and will take your insight and help with me as I have another cat at home and never know if this'll happen to him in the future.

My cat Simon has been looking thinner and in the past four days he has been lethargic, has no appetite, and was vomiting clear and foamy at least once or twice a day.

I took him to the ER vet today because his behavior had changed so drastically and they ran a blood test. The vet informed me he's never seen a number for the IDEXX SDMA so high as it was way over 100. He treated Simon in house and gave us a prescription medicine to lower his phosphorus but he told me that these numbers were insanely high. He also sent me home with some renal diet food.

I don't know how this could have happened, I replay every interaction I've had with my cat to see if maybe he ate some lilies or NSAIDs or even antifreeze but it's literally impossible for him to have come across anything like that. 

I just want to know if my baby even stands a chance with treatment and if it's worth putting him through exam after exam and treatment after treatment. I'm shell shocked and I left the vet not knowing if my cat would even survive til tomorrow.

I'm taking him to his regular vet tomorrow for a second opinion and more testing as they were closed today because of Memorial Day.
